text_rights.source_edition_note: The Wikisource page identifies the textual source as A. P. Chekhov, collected works, Nauka, Moscow, 1975, vol. 3, pp. 52–55 and 487. Only the story text is used; the 1975 edition's commentary, notes, introduction, layout, and scans are not copied. Any German scientific-edition related right under UrhG §70 would expire 25 years after the 1975 edition (by 2000), if that edition qualifies; the original story itself is not protected by copyright.
text_rights.translation: None. The source and BookCheef text are Russian.

jurisdiction_review.basis: Directive 2006/116/EC, Article 1(1) and calculation from 1 January following the relevant event (recital 15). Known individual author; no coauthors; first published during author's lifetime.
jurisdiction_review.calculation: Chekhov died 15 July 1904. Life plus 70 years ran through 31 December 1974; public domain from 1 January 1975.
jurisdiction_review.result: Underlying story is public domain; the Wikisource transcription is additionally licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

jurisdiction_review.basis: EU term plus German UrhG §64. The 1975 collected edition is not reproduced as a facsimile or with its apparatus. If the edition qualifies for the related right in §70, that right expires 25 years after publication.
jurisdiction_review.calculation: Any §70 right tied to the 1975 edition expired no later than 2000. The story's authorial term expired in 1974.
jurisdiction_review.result: Underlying story and text used are cleared for commercial reuse subject to CC BY-SA attribution.

jurisdiction_review.basis: Government.nl / Business.gov.nl guidance: copyright lasts 70 years after the creator's death, counted from 1 January of the following year.
jurisdiction_review.result: Underlying story is public domain; CC BY-SA 4.0 conditions for the digital transcription are retained.

jurisdiction_review.basis: Civil Code Part IV, Articles 1281 and 1282; Federal Law No. 231-FZ, Article 6 transitional rule.
jurisdiction_review.calculation: Chekhov's old 50-year term expired decades before 1 January 1993, so the 2006 transitional provision extending terms to 70 years does not revive it. Even the conservative life-plus-70 calculation would have ended on 31 December 1974.
jurisdiction_review.result: Underlying story is public domain; author name and integrity must still be respected.

jurisdiction_review.basis: The exact 1884 issue was published before 1 January 1931; the Commons file record marks the issue public domain in the United States.
jurisdiction_review.result: Underlying story is public domain in the United States.

jurisdiction_review.basis: The Wikisource transcription is under a worldwide CC BY-SA 4.0 license from contributors, but this record does not constitute a country-by-country legal opinion for every jurisdiction. The Commons PD template lists some longer-term jurisdictions generically; those listed terms (up to 100 years) would also have expired for an author who died in 1904, but no exhaustive global survey was completed.
jurisdiction_review.result: Do not represent this record as a legal opinion for every country. If BookCheef requires exhaustive worldwide certification, obtain manual legal review before global distribution.

edition_and_scan_review.original_issue_metadata: 1884, issue 36, Russian-language humor magazine Осколки; 8-page scan; Commons page identifies source as the National Electronic Library and displays Public Domain Mark 1.0, PD-Russia, and PD-US status.
edition_and_scan_review.reason: The scan is used only as bibliographic corroboration; no page image, scan, cover, or facsimile is embedded or redistributed. The BookCheef text comes from the licensed Wikisource transcription.
edition_and_scan_review.limitation: The National Electronic Library page itself could not be opened during this run; its record is cited only as the source named by the Commons file page. No scan file was downloaded or uploaded.
